chunks: And it is reported from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
Whenever one of you supplicates against anyone, he should say: 'O Allah, strike him with an affliction for which there is no equal, and crack his sanctity'.

key_terms.لَا أُخْتَ لَهَا: For which there is no equal/peer (unique)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to say against an enemy according to Imam Al-Reza?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication attributed to Imam al-Rida (AS) emphasizes the uniqueness of divine affliction by requesting a 'trial with no sister,' implying a singular, unparalleled hardship. It also invokes the 'breaking of the sanctum' (tahrīm), a concept linking physical or social protection to the loss of honor, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise linguistic nuance in du'a for justice against oppressors. This formula is often recited in contexts of personal grievance or spiritual warfare, balancing mercy with the removal of barriers to the enemy's well-being.

en.hubeali: And it is reported from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Whenever one of you supplicates against anyone, he should say, 
‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Strike him with an affliction there being no comparison for it, and crack his sanctity’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from abu al-Hassan (a.s.) who has said the following: “
When any of you prays against the other person he should say, ‘O Lord, strike him with peerless misfortune in the night and allow his defenses to be ransacked.’”
